- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model shows gradual upward trend, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast growth to +3–4% per day unless sentiment remains strong.
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model overestimates upside; apply downward bias of 1–2% to forecast mean.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is rising, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% downward adjustment to later forecast days.
- If multiple consecutive days show high bullish sentiment + high event count, model may overreact; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not just historical slope.
- When supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model often overestimates price; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days unless confirmed by new event.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may misread sentiment; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid false momentum.
